subject: Food Science
title: Why Bitter Exists
description: A micro-lesson that makes Why Bitter Exists usable.

hook.text: Humans have 25 different bitter taste receptors but only 1 for sweet. Evolution invested heavily in detecting poisons.

buildup.text: Plants produce bitter compounds—alkaloids, terpenes, and phenols—to deter herbivores. Bitter taste evolved as a warning system.

discovery.text: Caffeine, quinine, and nicotine are all bitter alkaloids. We override the warning signal because we learned their effects are.

twist.text: Children's extreme bitter sensitivity is protective—they can't judge what's safe.

climax.text: Many bitter compounds are healthy—flavonoids in dark chocolate, polyphenols in green tea, and glucosinolates in broccoli all.

punchline.text: Bitter evolved to warn you. But the things that taste bitter are often the healthiest.

quiz.question: Why do humans have 25 bitter receptors but only 1 sweet receptor?
options: Evolution prioritized detecting many different potential poisons
